selection_rationale: cand-003 (Workflow-Centered Evaluation of Generate→Validate→Repair Pipelines) best matches the track’s operational-focus: high novelty and falsifiability, direct measurement of end-to-end NetOps reliability metrics (safe-deploy, canary detection, rollback), feasible within stated compute/model budget, and strong relevance to NetOps governance and safety concerns. Its workflow-centered framing yields actionable insights beyond isolated correctness metrics, making it the strongest defensible short-paper contribution.
unresolved_uncertainties: Simulation realism and external validity: how well injected failures and simulated rollback policies map to real operator behavior and heterogeneous production devices.
Generalisability of canary-thresholds and detection tuning: risk of overfitting thresholds to the simulated failure distribution.
Validator coverage vs. real-world semantics: whether digital-twin checks detect the full class of semantic/policy failures (TOCTOU and emulator fidelity gaps).
Operational cost tradeoffs: delays/false-positives from pipeline stages (canary, repair, proofs) and their acceptability in live operations.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Document and publish the full simulation model (failure injection types, timing/TOCTOU models, rollback policy) and provide replay scripts for independent verification.
Include robustness checks in the preregistration: vary canary thresholds, injection rates, and rollback policies; specify the ranges and analysis plan for sensitivity reporting.
Justify and preregister the selection of injected failure types and their proportion (e.g., the 40% injection rate) with rationale tied to operational data or prior literature.
Preregister deterministic decision rules for automated rollback and a precise operational definition of ‘safe-deploy’ (including holdout semantic tests not exposed to the repair loop).
